questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

When the train pulled in/at the station, it take/Joseph some time/to get off.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is option 2) i.e. 'at the station, it take.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the part 'at the station, it take.'
 
• We can note that the first segment of the given sentence is in the past tense **'pulled in.'**
 
• The erroneous part contains the verb '**take'** which is in the present tense form, which is not consistent with the rest of the sentence that is written in the past tense.
 
• So we need to use the past form of the verb **'took.'**
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• **​***We **took** a roundabout route to avoid the accident.*
 
 
 
• Therefore in the given sentence, we need to use 'took' in place of 'take' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

 

Correct sentence:__* When the train pulled in **at the station, it __took__ **Joseph some time to get off. *

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

The government will build an amphitheatre.

options.text: An amphitheatre will be build by the government.
An amphitheatre will be built by the government.
An amphitheatre would be built by the government.
An amphitheatre be build by the government.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2) i.e. 'An amphitheatre will be built by the government. '

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the active voice. We have to change the sentence into passive form. 
 
• The given sentence is written in 'simple future tense.'
 
• The structure of these kinds of sentences is:
 
 
• Active Voice: Subject + will/shall + V1 + Object.
 
• Passive Voice: Object + will/shall + be + V3 + by (preposition) + Subject.
 
 
 
• Let’s see another example:
 
 
• Active voice: Shyam will write a poem.
 
• Passive voice: A poem will be written by Shyam.
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'The government' and the object of the given sentence is 'an amphitheatre'. 
 
• So, in the passive voice, the position of ‘subject’ and ‘object’ will be interchanged. 
 
• Also here, '**will build**' will be changed into 'will be built'.

 

Correct Sentence:__ *An amphitheatre will be built by the government. *

P. is timing, in particular ensuring that

Q. is essential to navigating deep space

R. the time on board spacecraft is synchronised

S. with the time on the ground

• Sentence Q is the first sentence as the paragraph begins with the subject **'One element that'** and therefore we have to use the verb **'is'** after it. The next part of the sentence is** "to navigating deep space," **which is a prepositional phrase that modifies the verb **"is essential."** This sets up the idea that the sentence is going to describe something that is crucial for navigating deep space.
 
• Sentence P is the second sentence as it begins with the helping verb **'is'** and explains what the essential element is. The essential element is timing. Thus it establishes a relation with the previous sentence.
 
• The only option that shows such an arrangement is **Option 4.**
 
• Sentence R is the third sentence as it begins with the noun 'the time' and mentions synchronizing the time on board spacecraft.
 
• Sentence S is the last sentence as it begins with the preposition 'with.' It tells us that it is important to ensure that the time on board the spacecraft is synchronized with the time on the ground thus it establishes a relation with the previous sentence.
